notes: 629 words, ten sections, two appendices. The document holds well over twelve legitimate facts, so the 12-fact budget must drop things and name what it dropped in skipped. The six required facts are the consequential ones: three dated commitments with owners, one dated decision with a decider, the money risk, and the quarter's compute spend. Everything else - throughput metrics, hiring metrics, all of Appendix A, all of Appendix B - is allowed but must not be required, and a run that fills its twelve slots with appendix trivia while dropping Priya's $240,000 risk has failed the ranking even though its recall looks fine. Traps planted: (1) the in-house storage decision that was discussed and explicitly not settled; (2) two false-gap traps on the postmortem date and the hiring plan owner; (3) Appendix A exists to bait the budget with five small, correct, worthless numbers; (4) 'Customer satisfaction is trending in the right direction' is a direction with no measure - a gap about it is expected and correct, but it is not required, because reasonable runs may rank other gaps above it in the top five.
